newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares finished at record highs, as players anticipated that positive money supply and private sector credit figures would point to a reduction in the country's high interest rates.
Financial shares also finished at record levels on the day.
"The market is looking for an indication for a rate cut," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollack told Reuters.
The main feature of the day was the demerger of gold mining firm Gencor and the seperate listing of its base metals arm Billiton Plc BILJ.J.

Billiton on Monday listed 1.66 billion shares and 426.70 million renounceable letters of entitlement on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, which shareholders are able to acquire through holding Gencor shares.

Traders said that there were vast differences of opinion between brokers on the pricing of Gencor following the unbundling and a one-for-five share consolidation. Valuations ranged in a wide 10.00 to 14.00 rand band.

Gencor plunged to 12.35 cents, a 33 percent drop from 18.45 rand, after hitting a low of 900 cents. Dealers said the drop was partly due to some players selling stock to withdraw from the firm's exposure to bullion, which recently hit its lowest level in 12 years.
Others said it was due to profit taking after players had bought into Gencor last week ahead of the unbundling.
Gold shares finished strong, boosted by a firmer bullion price which has been holding around the $326 per ounce level.

The financial index also finished at a new life high, up 31.9 points at 10,491.3. The industrial index gained 71.5 points to a record 9,125.9 points, lifting the all-share index up 46.8 points to a record 7,490.8 points.
Gold shares rose 21.0 points to 990.8 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues outpaced declining issues by 238 to 135 with 36 new highs and 15 new lows recorded.
Penny-stocks, those shares trading below a rand, were active after a Sunday newspaper tipped some as having potential to grow earnings substantially.
Investment trust Vestacor Ltd and electronics firm Usko Ltd were among the mostly actively traded penny stocks, adding four and three cents to 94 and 80 cents respectively.

Vestacor buys into quality companies with strong growth potential and nurtures them until they can be listed on the exchange while Usko has a strong balance sheet and plans to expand into high growth, hi-tech areas.

Another electronics firm, Jasco, gained 45 cents to 325 cents in a volume of nearly half a million shares helped by news that black empowerment grouping Capital Alliance Bank Ltd (Captall) had bought a 9.1 percent stake in the group.
Jasco also said that it had reached agreement with pharmaceutical firm Macmed to buy the businesses of those Jasco subsidiaries collectively known as the "scientific group".
The market was seen taking its cue from the money supply and credit extension figures due at the close of trade as well as consumer price inflation and trade figures due on Tuesday.

"Obviously direction will be determined by money supply and credit extension figures. It (the market) will also look towards CPI and trade data due tomorrow," Dominic Rey, international dealer at Investec Bank, said.
Near-dated equity index futures also ended strong on expectations of that the economic data would point to a reduction in interest rates.
Gold contracts finished firm on a better bullion price.
The September all-share contract was last at 6,738/45 from 6,711, the industrial contract was at 8,675/83 from 8,616 and the gold contract was at 695/710 from 677.
-- Charles Phahlane, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
